title: The Unexpected Ways Great Companies Show They Care About Their People
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article makes the case that occasional, unexpected, and non-transactional rewards carry more emotional weight with employees than routine, performance-linked recognition. It argues that the best gestures are extravagant in style rather than expense, are unconnected to any specific achievement, and are memorable enough that recipients want to share them. The piece offers a long list of concrete reward ideas and closes by reframing these gestures not as tools for building morale or loyalty, but as simple expressions that leaders genuinely care about the people who make the organization work.
points: Rewards that are unexpected and detached from specific performance carry outsized emotional impact compared to routine recognition.
The best rewards are extravagant in feel, not necessarily in cost, and prompt people to want to share the experience with others.
Suggested gestures range from surprise team experiences to personalized, high-touch perks unlikely to occur to employees themselves.
Occasional surprise rewards signal that leaders value people as people, not just as contributors to results.
The motivation behind these gestures should be genuine care, not a calculated strategy to boost morale or retention.
quotes: Some organizational rewards carry more weight because they are both unexpected and special.
The key is to do something unexpected that team members would be unlikely to do for themselves.
In fact, if team members don’t take and share photos of the reward, it probably wasn’t all that special.
This list of possible rewards is only limited by creativity.
Leaders don’t do it to create pride, to build team spirit, or to be recognized for their creativity. They do it because they care.
